page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core design. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile for this instance. Single-core CPU performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3111.68, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 3113.59 in stress-ng multi-core tests, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large block read and write operations at 47.32 GB/sec and 27.49 GB/sec respectively, while small block cached read bandwidth is weak at 153.15 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c8ae.large is its limited multi-core scaling and low memory capacity, as evidenced by weak PassMark CPU and database operation scores, the latter placing in the bottom 10%. Consequently, this instance is not suited for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized multi-threaded applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated, high-frequency single-core execution without large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and simple utility scripting.
